tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks after deploy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving regions mixed (us-east v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west v2.3.1). A retry finished the rollout. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: v2.3.1-rc was already unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production, so find out why it was promoted. Also look into the orchestrator partial-failure error.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

**Rollback**
- **What was broken:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Version chosen:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It has been healthy in production before, so the change-manager approval rule didn't apply.
- **Hiccup:** the first rollback stopped after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the other two regions on v2.3.1. I retried, since rolling back to the same version is safe to repeat, and the retry finished all three regions.
- **Now:** every region is on v2.3.0, healthy, with an error rate of about 0.2%.

**Incident**
- The first request to open it timed out. I retried with the same duplicate-protection key, and the incident list confirms only one incident exists.
- The incident describes what failed, the rollback and the partial failure. It also lists two follow-ups:
  - The test build of v2.3.1 was already failing health checks in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. Someone should find out why it was promoted.
  - The orchestrator error that stopped the first rollback needs looking into.

content.text: The rollback stopped partway: us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same version is safe to repeat, so I'll retry once.
